resources.string: Place the phone on a known level surface, keep it still, then set zero. The current position will become your reference.
Reading held • tap Release to continue

X/Y scales show inclination from −90° to +90°. The 0–360° ring and pointer show clockwise handset rotation relative to gravity: 0° top up, 90° right, 180° down, 270° left. This is not a compass. Hold the screen facing you, preferably upright. Rotation is undefined near flat and shown as a dash. X/Y zero calibration does not change the rotation reference.

Place the back of the phone against the surface. X measures left/right tilt; Y measures tilt along the phone. Bubbles move toward the higher side.

Calibrate only against a known level reference. The raised camera housing can tilt the phone: use a flat spacer or a straightedge. Hold freezes the displayed reading. Sound plays once when the selected vial settles within tolerance. Settings → Sound alignment mode: automatic, both axes, horizontal X, or vertical Y. Automatic uses both axes when flat, X with the top or bottom raised, and Y with a side raised. Long-press Sound to choose a mode. Enabling sound plays a preview. Phone volume buttons adjust media volume; Bluetooth or headphones may receive the sound.

The selected tolerance is an indication threshold, not a guaranteed accuracy. Check the phone by turning it 180° on the same surface. Avoid movement while measuring. Calibration and settings are stored locally. No Internet, ads, or tracking.
